title: He Took Eight Stitches to the Eye Mid-Shoot. Now Ram Charan's ₹339-Crore Epic Hits Netflix.
excerpt: Peddi, the Telugu sports drama that crowned Ram Charan as the 'New-Age Megastar,' premieres on Netflix July 9 in four languages. Here's why the Indian diaspora should clear their Wednesday evening.
body:
There's a moment in **Peddi** where the protagonist — a young man from an invisible village in Andhra Pradesh — amputates his own mangled leg, straps on a prosthetic blade, and runs. Not away from anything. Toward a promise he made to a dying friend. It's the kind of scene that either makes you roll your eyes or breaks you completely. Audiences in Hyderabad chose the second option: confetti, paper throws, standing ovations on opening day.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=sF2dj7ycZvA</youtube>

Now the rest of the world gets its turn. **Netflix** confirmed that *Peddi* will begin streaming on **July 9** in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam, with a Hindi version to follow. Five weeks after its June 4 theatrical release, the biggest Telugu film of 2026 is coming to your living room.

## The Numbers Tell One Story. The Film Tells Another.

At **₹338.98 crore worldwide**, *Peddi* is a commercial earthquake — the kind of number that turns a star into a franchise. But the more interesting story is what happened behind the camera.

At a post-release celebration, **Chiranjeevi** — Ram Charan's father and Telugu cinema's reigning Megastar — broke down recounting a near-disaster during an action sequence. Ram Charan took a hit to the eye that required **eight stitches**. Chiranjeevi said he only learned later how close the injury came to being something far worse. The elder star expressed relief mixed with unmistakable pride, then did something that sent the Telugu film world into overdrive: he publicly anointed his son as the **"New-Age Megastar."**

Coming from Chiranjeevi, that isn't fatherly affection. That's a coronation.

## The Underdog Who Runs on a Blade

Directed by **Buchi Babu Sana** — only his second feature — *Peddi* is set in the mid-1990s and follows a gifted sugarcane laborer from the Vizianagaram region. Born into an undocumented tribal community denied even a railway station, Peddi earns his keep as an *aata coolie* — a hired gun in local cricket tournaments. When tragedy strikes and a mentor's lifelong fight for the village ends in heartbreak, Peddi channels his grief into wrestling, rising through rural circuits with a raw physicality that can't be taught.

Then a rival's foul play shatters his leg. Career over. Story over — in a lesser film.

What follows is *Peddi*'s most audacious gambit: a one-legged athlete training on a prosthetic blade, entering national para-track competitions, and leveraging his victory to force the government to officially recognize his village. It's *Chariots of Fire* by way of *Rangasthalam*, with a social message that hit Telugu audiences right in the chest.

**A.R. Rahman** — the Oscar-winning composer who rarely signs Telugu films — provided a score that elevates the sports sequences into something almost mythic. **Janhvi Kapoor** plays the wealthy politician's daughter caught in the romance, while **Shiva Rajkumar**, **Divyenndu**, **Boman Irani**, and **Jagapathi Babu** fill out a cast designed for both drama and star power.

## Why the Diaspora Missed It — and Why That Changes Wednesday

Here's the thing about *Peddi* that the box-office reports don't fully capture: it **underperformed in overseas markets**. Telugu audiences in India embraced it overwhelmingly — theatres across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana turned into festivals on release day. But the diaspora largely missed the theatrical window. International screens were limited, and the film's Telugu-first marketing didn't cross language borders fast enough.

Netflix changes that equation entirely. Starting July 9, every Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam speaker in North America, the UK, the Gulf, and Australia can finally see what the fuss was about. The Hindi dub follows soon after, opening the door wider.

At three hours and two minutes, it's a commitment. At 5.9 on IMDb, it divides — critics found parts of it overwrought, fans found it transcendent. But the sheer physicality of Ram Charan's performance, the ambition of the underdog narrative, and Rahman's soaring score make a strong case for clearing your Wednesday evening.

## The Bottom Line

Ram Charan walked onto a set, took eight stitches to the face, and came back the next day. The character he plays cuts off his own leg and runs a national race. The line between actor and role blurred somewhere around the ₹300-crore mark — and Chiranjeevi noticed.

*Peddi* streams on Netflix from July 9. The Megastar has passed the torch. The blade runner is here.
author: Diaspora Desk
